plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets approximately 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but also limits upside potential. Expect lower drawdowns with this approach.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Trim QQQ to 15% and SMH to 5% to further reduce concentration.
Buy AAPL, targeting 4% of the book, based on its strong scanner setup.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for approximately 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Trim SPY to 25%, QQQ to 10%, and SMH to 5% to meet concentration mandates.
Add to SOXL, targeting 6%, and SPAL, targeting 6%, to lean into leveraged ETFs.
Buy AAPL, targeting 6% of the book, based on its strong scanner setup.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware this approach carries substantially higher drawdown risk and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay and rebalancing, potentially leading to rapid losses without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to prioritize income and low drawdown.
Trim QQQ to 10% and SMH to 5% to further reduce concentration and high-beta exposure.
income.read: This income plan targets approximately 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index funds. Remember, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
